reason: When the Hebrew people confront Moses and Aaron after their initial intervention worsens conditions, saying 'May the Lord look upon you and judge you, for you have made us repulsive in the eyes of Pharaoh' (Exodus 5:21), Moses does not take accountability or apologize. Instead, he goes to God and questions Him: 'Lord, why have you brought trouble on this people?...Since I came to Pharaoh...he has brought more trouble on this people; and you have not rescued your people.' Moses deflects responsibility to God rather than acknowledging his role in the worsening situation or answering to the people. The narrative shows Moses and Aaron continuing their mission as God's intermediaries, but they do not explicitly accept responsibility for the consequences or address the people's suffering with accountability.
